rows.en: Slowly becoming a puddle in the corner.
rows.reason: 'Kancane ngiba yichibi' says 'a little, I become a pond', and the melting is lost. A speaker would say 'kancane kancane' for 'gradually' and name the melting so the heat comes through.
rows.rewrite: Kancane kancane ngiyancibilika, ngiba yichibi ekhoneni.

rows.en: The sky picked a vibe and the vibe is shrug.
rows.draft: Isibhakabhaka sikhethe i-vibe futhi i-vibe iwukunyusa amahlombe.
rows.reason: 'ukunyusa amahlombe' is the real Zulu gesture for a shrug, and the i-vibe code-switch matches kept lines ('I-vibe yi-beige'). The joke is a little flat but intact.

rows.en: Hair plans: cancelled.
rows.reason: 'zikhanselelwe' is the applied form ('cancelled for someone'); the plain passive is 'zikhanselwe'. The rest is fine.
rows.rewrite: Izinhlelo zezinwele: zikhanselwe.

rows.en: The duvet understood the assignment.
rows.reason: 'iyiqondile into edingekayo' ('understood the thing that is needed') is stiff and loses the idiom. A speaker would say the duvet knows its job.
rows.rewrite: I-duvet iyawazi umsebenzi wayo.

rows.en: The garden is somewhere out there. We trust the process.
rows.reason: 'Somewhere' (endaweni ethile) is dropped, and that word carries the fog joke. 'Sithemba inqubo' is a bureaucratic calque ('we trust the procedure').
rows.rewrite: Ingadi ikhona ngaphandle, endaweni ethile. Siyakholwa nje.

rows.en: Perfect excuse to cancel plans.
rows.reason: Natural, plain phrasing. 'Isizathu esihle' carries the welcome-excuse sense well.

rows.en: This is why we live in South Africa.
rows.reason: Natural 'Yingakho…', the same shape as the confirmed 'Yingakho uNowa wakha umkhumbi'. The brag reads warm.

rows.en: It is what it is.
rows.reason: 'Kuyilokho okuyikho' is a word-for-word calque of the English. The everyday Zulu shrug is 'Kunjalo nje'.
rows.rewrite: Kunjalo nje.

rows.en: Sky's looking moody. Could escalate.
rows.reason: 'sithukuthele' works for a moody sky, but 'Kungakhula' ('it could grow') is vague for 'escalate'. A speaker would say it could get even worse.
rows.rewrite: Isibhakabhaka sibukeka sithukuthele. Kungaba kubi nakakhulu.

rows.en: Hold onto your hat! And your kids.
rows.reason: Direct and natural. The tag 'Nabantwana bakho' lands the second beat cleanly.

rows.en: Not a hairstyle in sight. Just survivors.
rows.draft: Akukho sitayela sezinwele esibonwayo. Abasindile kuphela.
rows.reason: Mirrors the confirmed 'Akukho lifu elibonwayo'. 'isitayela sezinwele' is the natural loan, and 'Abasindile kuphela' turns well.

rows.en: Clear-ish night. Don't hold us to the stars.
rows.reason: 'obuhle-ish' is a forced English suffix (the natives strip these, as with 'Lekker koud'), and 'obuhle' means nice, not clear. 'Ungasibambi ezinkanyezini' ('don't catch us in the stars') is a broken calque of 'hold us to'.
rows.rewrite: Ubusuku obucwebile, cishe. Asithembisi lutho ngezinkanyezi.

rows.en: A proper good one. Don't waste it.
rows.reason: 'olungcono' means 'the better one', not 'a good one', and the noun usuku is missing, so the reader has to guess what is meant.
rows.rewrite: Usuku oluhle ngempela. Ungalumoshi.

rows.en: Unplug the things. The sky has plans.
rows.draft: Susa izinto eziphakwe ku-elektriki. Isibhakabhaka sinezinhlelo.
rows.reason: 'eziphakwe' (phaka = to dish up) is the wrong word for 'plugged in', and 'elektriki' is forced where Zulu says ugesi or just the loan 'plug'. The second sentence is fine.
rows.rewrite: Khipha izinto ku-plug. Isibhakabhaka sinezinhlelo.

rows.en: The street signs gave up.
rows.reason: 'Izimpawu zomgwaqo' is the right term, and the personified 'ziyekile' (they quit) lands the fog joke.

rows.en: This is not what the tourism brochure promised.
rows.reason: 'incwadi yokuvakasha' reads as 'a visiting book or letter', not a tourism brochure. People would just say the loan.
rows.rewrite: Lokhu akukhona okwethenjiswa yi-brochure yezokuvakasha.

rows.en: The shower was the highlight. It is downhill from here.
rows.draft: Ishawa kwakuyinto enhle. Konke kuya phansi manje.
rows.reason: 'kwakuyinto enhle' ('was a nice thing') loses 'highlight' and has a stray ku- concord. 'Konke kuya phansi manje' is a stiff literal take on 'downhill from here'.
rows.rewrite: Okuhle kakhulu namuhla bekuyishawa. Kusukela manje kuya ngokuya kuba kubi.

rows.en: Tile floors are tonight's villain. Wear something on your feet.
rows.draft: Ama-tile floors yi-villain yanamuhla kusihlwa. Gqoka okuthile ezinyaweni.
rows.reason: 'Ama-tile floors' keeps the English plural (the natives fixed 'ama-rugby fields' the same way), and 'yanamuhla kusihlwa' is clunky for 'tonight'.
rows.rewrite: Amathayela ayisitha salobu busuku. Gqoka okuthile ezinyaweni.

rows.en: Shorts weather? This is underwear weather.
rows.draft: Isimo sezulu samabhulukwe amafushane? Lesi isimo sezulu samangisi.
rows.reason: 'amangisi' is not a word I can confirm for underwear (it reads invented), and 'Lesi isimo' is missing its copula (should be 'Lesi yisimo').
rows.rewrite: Isimo sezulu samabhulukwe amafushane? Cha, lesi yisimo sezulu sezingubo zangaphansi.

rows.en: Boerie roll for breakfast? On a weekend? Acceptable.
rows.reason: 'ibhulakufesi' and 'Ngempelasonto' are natural, and the three-beat build lands. The only slip is that 'Iboerie' wants a hyphen ('I-boerie').

rows.en: Beach or braai? Yes.
rows.reason: Uses the natives' own 'ukosa' and 'ibhishi'. The 'Yebo' answer to an either-or works just as in English.

rows.en: Beautiful and terrifying in equal measure.
rows.reason: Clean, natural Zulu. 'ngokulinganayo' carries 'in equal measure' exactly.

rows.en: Even the shade is sweating.
rows.reason: Natural and tight: 'ngisho nomthunzi uyajuluka' personifies the shade exactly as the English does.

rows.en: Looks cold-ish. The thermometer's keeping us guessing.
rows.reason: 'Kubukeka kubanda' follows the kept 'Kubukeka kunamafu' pattern; 'i-thermometer isenza siqagele' is everyday code-switched isiZulu. The '-ish' softness is lost, as in kept low-confidence lines.

rows.en: The N1 is now a waterpark.
rows.reason: Short and natural code-switch; place name and 'waterpark' stay as people say them, and the flooded-road joke lands.

rows.en: Clouds looking proper suspicious.
rows.reason: '-solisa' (look suspicious) is the same word natives kept in 'okusolisayo'; 'ngempela' carries 'proper'. Clouds as a character works.

rows.en: The fog doesn't care about your schedule.
rows.reason: 'isheduli' is a forced loan where isiZulu says 'izinhlelo' (as in the kept 'Izinhlelo zanamuhla'); 'ayinandaba' is the everyday way to say 'doesn't care'.
rows.rewrite: Inkungu ayinandaba nezinhlelo zakho.

rows.en: The puddle was deeper than it looked. It's always deeper.
rows.draft: Isiziba sasijule kunalokho ebesibukeka ngakho. Sihlala sijule.
rows.reason: 'kunalokho ebesibukeka ngakho' is stiff and translated, and mixes remote past 'sasijule' with recent past 'ebesibukeka'; a speaker would say 'kunendlela ebesibukeka ngayo'. The second beat needs 'kunalokho' to keep 'always deeper'.
rows.rewrite: Isiziba besijule kunendlela ebesibukeka ngayo. Sihlala sijule kunalokho.

rows.en: The sky's undecided. So are we.
rows.reason: Clean two-beat turn; 'Nathi futhi' is slightly redundant but natural enough, close to the kept 'Asazi nathi'.

rows.en: 50/50 on the rain. Bring a jacket, just in case.
rows.draft: I-50/50 emvuleni. Thatha ibhantshi, uma kwenzeka.
rows.reason: 'I-50/50 emvuleni' reads 'a 50/50 in the rain' (locative = out in the rain), not 'the rain is 50/50'; a speaker would make the rain the subject.
rows.rewrite: Imvula i-50/50. Thatha ibhantshi, uma kwenzeka.

rows.en: Good soup weather, not gonna lie.
rows.reason: Same shape as the kept 'Isimo sezulu esihle sefilimu yesabisayo'; 'isobho' is right. The 'not gonna lie' beat is dropped, so it reads warm rather than funny.

rows.en: Don't trust those clouds. They're plotting.
rows.reason: 'Ungawathembi lawo mafu. Ayaceba.' is natural; '-ceba' (to scheme) is the exact word for plotting clouds.

rows.en: Even the shade is warm. Good luck out there.
rows.reason: Natural first beat; 'Inhlanhla enhle' is the same sign-off natives kept elsewhere. 'Out there' is dropped, but the line still reads warm.

rows.en: Wait it out indoors. The mountains aren't going anywhere.
rows.reason: 'Lindela phakathi' is off: 'lindela' needs an object (wait for something) and indoors is 'ngaphakathi'. 'Izintaba aziyi ndawo' is good and stays.
rows.rewrite: Linda ngaphakathi kuze kudlule. Izintaba aziyi ndawo.

rows.en: Postcard weather. You're welcome.
rows.reason: 'se-postcard' is a natural loan and 'Wamukelekile' is the same tag natives kept in 'Bheka phezulu. Wamukelekile.' The cheeky 'you're welcome' reads softer in isiZulu.

rows.en: Your jacket has a jacket. It's that kind of day.
rows.reason: The joke is the repeated word: 'ijazi ... ibhantshi' reads as 'your coat has a jacket', so the echo is lost. 'Usuku olunjalo' is a fragment; a speaker would say 'Kunjalo namuhla'.
rows.rewrite: Ijazi lakho linejazi lalo. Kunjalo namuhla.

rows.en: Cloudy-ish. Don't bet the braai on it.
rows.reason: 'Ungabhejeli ukosa kukho' is a calque with a dangling 'kukho'. To stake the braai is 'ungabheji ngokosa', and 'kulokhu' makes 'on it' clear.
rows.rewrite: Kunamafu, cishe. Ungabheji ngokosa kulokhu.

rows.en: Everyone's suddenly your friend when you have a pool.
rows.reason: 'Suddenly' carries the joke and is dropped, so 'Bonke bangabangane bakho' is just a flat statement. 'ipuli' is an odd spelling; people say 'i-pool'.
rows.rewrite: Bonke bavele babe ngabangane bakho uma une-pool.

rows.en: Today's forecast: medium rare.
rows.reason: 'Medium rare' stays in English the way urban speakers order a steak, like the kept 'liku-airplane mode'. The punchline survives.

rows.en: Even the weather apps are arguing about this one.
rows.reason: Natural: 'ama-app ezulu ayaphikisana ngalokhu' is how people would say it, and arguing apps match the app's own 'probably' voice.

rows.en: Might spit a bit. Might not bother.
rows.reason: '-khihliza' means spitting saliva, not light rain; isiZulu says 'ukukhemezela' for drizzle. 'Kungahluphi' means 'won't trouble (you)', but the joke is 'won't bother itself': 'kungazihluphi'.
rows.rewrite: Kungakhemezela kancane. Noma kungazihluphi.

rows.en: Not the time for hero moves, hey.
rows.reason: 'sokuqhawe' is not a word (heroism is 'ubuqhawe'); 'hero moves' is 'ukuzenza iqhawe' (playing the hero).
rows.rewrite: Akusona isikhathi sokuzenza iqhawe, hey.

rows.en: Joburg drivers are panicking already.
rows.reason: Natural and short; 'sebeyesaba' (already scared) is close enough to 'panicking', and the Joburg-drivers jab lands.

rows.en: Bloemfontein at 6am: jersey, gown, scarf, takkies, and a brave face.
rows.draft: EBloemfontein ngo-6 ekuseni: i-jersey, i-gown, i-scarf, ama-takkies, nobuso obunesibindi.
rows.reason: Too many forced loans where isiZulu has its own everyday words: jersey is 'ijezi' (the pack's own correction) and scarf is 'isikhafu'. 'i-gown' and 'ama-takkies' stay as people say them.
rows.rewrite: EBloemfontein ngo-6 ekuseni: ijezi, i-gown, isikhafu, ama-takkies, nobuso obunesibindi.

rows.en: Your excuse to stay inside just expired.
rows.draft: Isizathu sakho sokuhlala ngaphakathi sisanda kuphelelwa.
rows.reason: 'sisanda kuphelelwa' is incomplete ('has just run out of ...'); 'expired' needs 'yisikhathi'. Natives use 'izaba' for excuses ('Ngisho nezaba zakho'), not 'isizathu' (reason).
rows.rewrite: Izaba zakho zokuhlala ngaphakathi seziphelelwe yisikhathi.

rows.en: Not a cloud. Just you and the Southern Cross.
rows.draft: Akukho lifu. Nguwe neSiphambano saseNingizimu kuphela.
rows.reason: "Isiphambano saseNingizimu" is a calque that can read as 'the southern crossroads'; speakers just say the Southern Cross by its name.
rows.rewrite: Akukho lifu. Nguwe nje ne-Southern Cross.

rows.en: The trees are doing involuntary yoga.
rows.reason: "engafuneki" means 'unwanted', not 'involuntary'; the joke is that the trees do it against their will.
rows.rewrite: Izihlahla zenza i-yoga zingathandi.

rows.en: Perfect weather for existing without enthusiasm.
rows.draft: Isimo sezulu esihle sokuphila ngaphandle kwentshisekelo.
rows.reason: "ukuphila ngaphandle kwentshisekelo" is formal, sermon-like ('living without zeal'); a speaker would say just being there with no umdlandla.
rows.rewrite: Isimo sezulu esihle sokuba khona nje, ungenamdlandla.

rows.en: SPF 50 or regret it by tonight.
rows.reason: Natural warning-plus-consequence, same shape as the kept 'Sebenzisa futhi noma uhlupheke'; 'ngokuhlwa' is the right time word.

rows.en: Perfect weather for a Woolies run and Netflix.
rows.reason: Same terse 'isimo sezulu esihle se-' pattern natives kept; brand names stay as they are and an SA reader gets the trip.

rows.en: Even the cattle on the N1 are huddled like they paid for it.
rows.draft: Ngisho nezinkomo eziku-N1 zibuthene sengathi zikhokhele indawo.
rows.reason: Natural; 'sengathi zikhokhele indawo' turns the huddle into paid-for seats, so the joke lands.

rows.en: Stay hydrated or become a biltong.
rows.reason: "Hlala unamanzi" reads 'stay with water / stay wet', not 'stay hydrated'; a speaker says drink water.
rows.rewrite: Phuza amanzi njalo noma uphenduke i-biltong.

rows.en: Water consumption: yes. All of it.
rows.reason: "Konke" reads as 'everything'; 'all of it' for the water is 'wonke amanzi', which keeps the exaggeration.
rows.rewrite: Ukuphuza amanzi: yebo. Wonke amanzi akhona.

rows.en: Somewhere a weather reporter is living their best life.
rows.draft: Endaweni ethile umethuli wezindaba zesimo sezulu uphila kahle.
rows.reason: "uphila kahle" means 'is keeping well / is healthy', not 'living their best life'; 'umethuli wezindaba zesimo sezulu' is long-winded.
rows.rewrite: Endaweni ethile, umethuli wesimo sezulu uyazitika namuhla.

rows.en: Kite surfers are having the time of their lives.
rows.reason: "abadlali be-kite" pictures people flying toy kites, not kite surfers; 'bajabulile kakhulu' is flat for 'time of their lives'.
rows.rewrite: Abadlali be-kitesurfing bayazitika impela namuhla.

rows.en: Sunscreen budget: higher than your data bill.
rows.draft: Isabiwezimali sesivikelo selanga: siphezulu kunebhili yakho yedatha.
rows.reason: "Isabiwezimali" is a stiff budget-speech word (and an odd form of isabelomali); people just say i-budget.
rows.rewrite: I-budget yesivikelo selanga: iphezulu kunebhili yakho yedatha.

rows.en: The UV index is higher than your expectations.
rows.reason: Natural and correct; the tease about low expectations softens to a plain 'higher than you expect', but nothing is wrong.

rows.en: The Helderberg is showing off today.
rows.reason: Same verb natives kept for the brag ('iyaziqhayisa'); place name stays as is.

rows.en: The sky's on mute. Nobody's complaining.
rows.reason: 'sithulile' (gone silent) is a fair image for 'on mute' and 'Akekho okhonondayo' is idiomatic; the device gag is softer.

rows.en: The sun doesn't care about your plans.
rows.reason: 'alikhathali' is the everyday 'doesn't care'; reads like something a speaker would say.

rows.en: Kuier weather. Get the people together.
rows.reason: Warm and natural; 'sokuhlangana' carries kuier and 'Biza abantu' is a plain, real invitation.

rows.en: The bins are on an adventure again.
rows.reason: 'asohambweni' gives the bins a trip with a dry deadpan; natural loan 'amabhini'.

rows.en: Trust issues with the sky today.
rows.reason: "Inkinga yokuthemba isibhakabhaka" is a stiff noun phrase ('a problem of trusting the sky'); urban speakers say trust issues as is.
rows.rewrite: Sinama-trust issues nesibhakabhaka namuhla.

rows.en: Probably a scorcher. A hat's not a bad idea.
rows.draft: Cishe usuku olushisayo. Isigqoko asilona icebo elibi.
rows.reason: Correct and clear, matches the kept 'Cishe usuku ...' low-confidence lines; a touch literal but nothing wrong.

rows.en: Cloud's the call. With an asterisk.
rows.reason: "Amafu yiwo umbono" ('the clouds are the opinion') is awkward and "Kanye nophawu" ('with a mark') means nothing to a reader; the caveat is lost.
rows.rewrite: Sithi kuzoba namafu. Kodwa asifungi.

rows.en: The fridge is the coolest room in the house.
rows.draft: Ifriji iyindawo epholile kunayo yonke endlini.
rows.reason: Superlative should be plural ('kunawo/kunazo zonke'), not 'kunayo yonke'; 'igumbi' keeps the fridge-as-a-room joke.
rows.rewrite: Ifriji yigumbi elipholile kunawo wonke endlini.

rows.en: Even the weather can't be bothered today.
rows.draft: Ngisho nesimo sezulu asikwazi ukuziphatha namuhla.
rows.reason: "asikwazi ukuziphatha" means 'can't behave itself', not 'can't be bothered'; the lazy weather becomes misbehaving weather.
rows.rewrite: Ngisho nesimo sezulu asizihluphi namuhla.

rows.en: Whoever has a pool today is your new best friend.
rows.draft: Noma ngubani onepuli namuhla ngumngane wakho omusha omkhulu.
rows.reason: "ipuli" is not how speakers say pool (loans take ph-, and people just say i-pool); 'omusha omkhulu' reads better as 'omkhulu omusha'.
rows.rewrite: Noma ngubani one-pool namuhla ngumngane wakho omkhulu omusha.

rows.en: The chops are calling. So is the chair.
rows.reason: 'Nesihlalo nawo' means 'and the chair with them' (nawo agrees with ama-chop), not 'so is the chair'; the chair needs its own verb: nesihlalo siyabiza.
rows.rewrite: Ama-chop ayabiza. Nesihlalo siyabiza.

rows.en: The ozone layer called. It's on leave.
rows.reason: 'ishayile' on its own reads 'it hit' or 'it knocked off work', not 'it called'; a speaker says ishaye ucingo, and 'ise-leave' sits more naturally after it.
rows.rewrite: I-ozone layer ishaye ucingo. Ithi ise-leave.

rows.en: The weather gods are showing off.
rows.reason: 'Izinkulunkulu zesimo sezulu' is a word-for-word 'gods of the weather condition', stiff and odd; a speaker makes the sky itself the show-off (izulu liyaziqhayisa, like the confirmed imvelo iyaziqhayisa).
rows.rewrite: Izulu liyaziqhayisa namuhla.

rows.en: The wipers are on max and it's still not enough.
rows.reason: Natural urban code-switch (ama-wipers, aku-max); 'kodwa akwanele' is the same turn natives kept in the socks line.

rows.en: The dog is staring at the rain like it's a personal insult.
rows.draft: Inja ibheka imvula sengathi inhlamba yomuntu siqu.
rows.reason: 'sengathi inhlamba' lacks the copula (yinhlamba) and 'ibheka' is just 'looks'; a speaker says the dog stares (igqolozele) as if the rain insulted it (iyithukile).
rows.rewrite: Inja igqolozele imvula sengathi iyithukile.

rows.en: Don't even think about driving somewhere.
rows.reason: 'ngisho ngokushayela ndawo' is off: ngisho wants na-, and ndawo needs a going verb; a speaker says 'ungacabangi nhlobo ukushayela uye ndawo'.
rows.rewrite: Ungacabangi nhlobo ukushayela uye ndawo.

rows.en: Grey vibes. The sky matched my Monday.
rows.draft: I-grey vibes. Isibhakabhaka sifana noMsombuluko wami.
rows.reason: Code-switched 'i-grey vibes' matches the natives' i-vibe lines; 'sifana noMsombuluko wami' is plain and lands.

rows.en: Weather's being more indecisive than you at Spur.
rows.draft: Isimo sezulu asikwazi ukuzinquma njengawe eSpur.
rows.reason: 'ukuzinquma' is the reflexive (cut/decide oneself); 'make up its mind' is ukunquma, as in the confirmed 'asikwazi ukunquma'; 'uma use-Spur' reads more naturally than bare eSpur.
rows.rewrite: Isimo sezulu asikwazi ukunquma, njengawe uma use-Spur.

rows.en: Good day for a walk, bad day for a tan.
rows.reason: 'lokushisa' means 'for heat/burning', not 'for a tan'; a tan here is basking in the sun, ukuthamela ilanga.
rows.rewrite: Usuku oluhle lokuzihambela, kodwa olubi lokuthamela ilanga.

rows.en: Not Instagram weather. Not the end of the world.
rows.draft: Akusona isimo sezulu se-Instagram. Akusikho ukuphela komhlaba.
rows.reason: Correct copulatives (akusona, akusikho) and the everyday phrase 'ukuphela komhlaba'; the two flat beats keep the shrug.

rows.en: The clouds are here but they're not doing anything.
rows.reason: Exactly how a speaker says it; 'awenzi lutho' carries the lazy-cloud joke.

rows.en: Probably quiet skies. We're fairly sure.
rows.reason: Plain, natural low-confidence line; 'Siqinisekile cishe' is the natives' own phrase.

rows.en: Don't touch the seatbelt buckle. Trust us.
rows.reason: 'ibhakili' is not a word people use (they say i-buckle), and a seatbelt is 'ibhande lokuphepha', not 'lokuvikela'; ibhakili also drags the object concord to li-.
rows.rewrite: Ungayithinti i-buckle yebhande lokuphepha. Sithembe.

rows.en: Stars out, load shedding can't touch this.
rows.reason: 'ukucisha akukwazi lokhu' reads 'switching-off does not know this' (kwazi = know); load shedding is said as i-load shedding, and 'can't touch' needs ukuzithinta.
rows.rewrite: Izinkanyezi ziphumile, i-load shedding ayikwazi ukuzithinta.

rows.en: The clouds are committed to being average.
rows.reason: 'zibophezele' (committed) against 'phakathi naphakathi' (middling) keeps the dry contradiction intact.

rows.en: This is the weather you'll miss in December traffic.
rows.draft: Lesi yisimo sezulu ozosithanda ethrafikhini kaDisemba.
rows.reason: 'ozosithanda' means 'you will love it', not 'you will miss it'; miss is ozosikhumbula, which restores the joke.
rows.rewrite: Lesi yisimo sezulu ozosikhumbula usethrafikhini kaDisemba.

rows.en: The kind of cold that has you Googling 'underfloor heating Bloemfontein'.
rows.draft: Uhlobo lwamakhaza olukwenza ugcine usu-Google'a 'underfloor heating Bloemfontein'.
rows.reason: 'Uhlobo lwamakhaza olukwenza' follows the natives' 'uhlobo losuku olwenza'; the Googled phrase stays in English as it would.

rows.en: At least it's not raining. That's the bar.
rows.reason: 'Yilokho okukhona' says 'that is what there is', losing 'that's the bar' (the low standard); 'akulini' is also an unusual form where speakers say imvula ayini or akuni.
rows.rewrite: Okungenani imvula ayini. Lelo yizinga lethu namuhla.

rows.en: Thunder rolling in. Inside is the move.
rows.reason: 'Hlala phakathi' can read 'stay in the middle'; indoors is ngaphakathi (as in the confirmed 'Hlala ngaphakathi!'), and thunder is ukuduma kwezulu.
rows.rewrite: Ukuduma kwezulu kuyeza. Hlala ngaphakathi.

rows.en: The world got a soft filter this morning.
rows.reason: Natural, and 'ifilitha ethambile' is a clean picture of the fog; ekuseni does the 'this morning' work.

rows.en: Slip-slops, shorts, sun. The trinity.
rows.draft: Izimbadada, amabhulukwe amafushane, ilanga. Inhlangano emithathu.
rows.reason: 'Inhlangano emithathu' is 'organisation' with a wrong concord (emithathu is class 4; inhlangano needs entathu), and it is not 'trinity'; the list beat is fine.
rows.rewrite: Izimbadada, amabhulukwe amafushane, ilanga. Izinto ezintathu ezingcwele.

rows.en: Wet conditions, probably. Don't quote us at the braai.
rows.reason: 'okosa' is a relative ('who braais'), not 'at the braai'; a speaker says ebraai, as the natives use braai elsewhere.
rows.rewrite: Izimo ezimanzi, cishe. Ungasicaphuni ebraai.

rows.en: Good night, South Africa.
rows.reason: 'Hamba kahle' means goodbye/go well (also the farewell said to the dead), not good night; it reads as a farewell to the country.
rows.rewrite: Lalani kahle, Ningizimu Afrika.

rows.en: Frost on the lawn. Frost on the bakkie. Frost in the pet bowl.
rows.draft: Isithwathwa otshanini. Isithwathwa ku-bakkie. Isithwathwa ku-pet bowl.
rows.reason: Triple rhythm works and 'isithwathwa otshanini' is right, but 'ku-pet bowl' is a forced English compound where isiZulu has its own words, the same fault natives fixed in 'milk bottle' and 'bird feeder'.
rows.rewrite: Isithwathwa otshanini. Isithwathwa ku-bakkie. Isithwathwa esitsheni senja.

rows.en: The umbrella tax is now in effect.
rows.reason: 'Intela yesambulela isiyasebenza' is clean and natural; the mock-official tax joke comes through as dryly as the English.

rows.en: Rain so heavy it should pay rent.
rows.draft: Imvula enzima kakhulu kufanele ikhokhe irenti.
rows.reason: 'Imvula enzima' is translated (heavy rain is 'enamandla'/'enkulu'), and without 'kangangokuthi' the so-that link is lost: it reads 'very heavy rain must pay rent'.
rows.rewrite: Imvula inamandla kangangokuthi kumele ikhokhe irenti.

rows.en: Time to dig out that ugly beanie.
rows.reason: 'ukumba' is to dig in the ground, a calque of 'dig out'; a speaker says 'ukukhipha' (take out), and the line needs 'sekuyisikhathi'.
rows.rewrite: Sekuyisikhathi sokukhipha leya beanie embi.

rows.en: This weather needs a life coach.
rows.draft: Lesi simo sezulu sidinga umqeqeshi wempilo.
rows.reason: Natural, correct concords; 'umqeqeshi wempilo' carries life coach and the weather-as-character joke lands.

rows.en: The Weber's been waiting all week for this.
rows.reason: 'ibelinde' is off for class 9 (past continuous is 'ibilinde'/'ibikade ilinde'), 'loku' should be 'lokhu', and the object sits better next to the verb.
rows.rewrite: I-Weber ibikade ilinde lokhu isonto lonke.

rows.en: Your breath is doing special effects.
rows.reason: 'umphefumulo' is read as soul/life, not visible breath, so it says 'your soul is doing special effects'; also 'ama-special effects' needs the plural.
rows.rewrite: Umoya ophuma emlonyeni wakho wenza ama-special effects.

rows.en: This is the day the brochure was talking about.
rows.reason: Missing copula: 'Lolu usuku' is 'this day', not 'this is the day'; a speaker says 'Yilolu usuku ...'.
rows.rewrite: Yilolu usuku incwajana ebikhuluma ngalo.

rows.en: The neighbours' pool has never looked so tempting.
rows.draft: Ipuli yomakhelwane ayikaze ibukeke ihehekayo kangaka.
rows.reason: 'ihehekayo' means easily tempted, not tempting ('iheha'); 'ipuli' is an odd spelling where people just say i-pool.
rows.rewrite: I-pool yomakhelwane ayikaze ibukeke iheha kangaka.

rows.en: The frogs have entered the chat.
rows.reason: 'Amasele angene engxoxweni' is natural and works even without the meme: croaking frogs joining the conversation.

rows.en: Probably cold. Take the jersey, you'll thank us.
rows.reason: Natural and warm; 'ijezi' is the right word and 'uzosibonga' carries the friendly nudge.

rows.en: Some cloud, some sun. The ratio's anyone's guess.
rows.draft: Amafu akhona, ilanga likhona. Isilinganiso siwukuqagela.
rows.reason: First half is fine; 'Isilinganiso siwukuqagela' is stiff, technical 'ratio' language a speaker would not use for the sky.
rows.rewrite: Amafu akhona, nelanga likhona. Ukuthi yikuphi okuningi, akekho owaziyo.

rows.en: Ja, it's jersey weather. Double jersey.
rows.draft: Yebo, yisikhathi sejezi. Ijezi ephindwe kabili.
rows.reason: 'Ijezi ephindwe kabili' has the wrong concord (ijezi is class 5: 'eli-') and 'doubled jersey' is stiff; a speaker says two jerseys, like 'ama-fleece amabili'.
rows.rewrite: Yebo, yisikhathi sejezi. Amajezi amabili.

rows.en: Can't see a thing. Not a thing.
rows.reason: 'Angiboni lutho. Lutho.' is exactly how a speaker says it; the emphatic echo works.

rows.en: At least the garden's happy. Someone has to be.
rows.draft: Okungenani ingadi iyajabula. Othile kumele ajabule.
rows.reason: 'Okungenani ingadi iyajabula' is natural; the turn 'othile kumele ajabule' keeps the dry second beat.

rows.en: Rooibos consumption just doubled.
rows.reason: The report-speak 'ukusetshenziswa' matches the mock-statistic English, and 'kusanda kuphindeka kabili' follows the natives' kept 'kuphindeka kathathu'.

rows.en: The moon's doing the most tonight.
rows.reason: 'yenza konke' means 'does everything', a calque of 'doing the most' that loses the overdoing/showing-off meaning.
rows.rewrite: Inyanga iyaziqhayisa namhlanje ebusuku.

rows.en: Weekend vibes so strong they need their own playlist.
rows.draft: I-weekend vibes ezinamandla kakhulu zidinga i-playlist yazo.
rows.reason: Concord clash: singular 'I-weekend vibes' with plural 'ezinamandla ... zidinga ... yazo'; the corpus uses 'ama-vibes', and 'kangangokuthi' is needed for 'so strong they'.
rows.rewrite: Ama-vibes e-weekend anamandla kangangokuthi adinga i-playlist yawo.

rows.en: Warm enough to leave the window open. Brave enough?
rows.reason: 'ngokwanele' is translated 'enough', and 'ukuvula' is to open, not to leave open, which is where the dare lives.
rows.rewrite: Kufudumele kangangokuthi ungashiya ifasitela livuliwe. Unesibindi?

rows.en: Nobody's posting this sunset on Instagram.
rows.reason: Natural, but 'lokhu' drops the sunset, so the dusk joke loses its object.
rows.rewrite: Akekho ozoposta lokhu kushona kwelanga ku-Instagram.

rows.en: Karoo morning. The kind that makes you respect every farmer who chose this.
rows.draft: Ekuseni eKaroo. Uhlobo olwenza uhloniphe wonke umlimi okhethe lokhu.
rows.reason: Follows the natives' kept 'Uhlobo losuku olwenza ...' pattern; 'uhloniphe' is correct and the respect for the farmer reads warm.

rows.en: Windows closed, kettle on, and wait.
rows.reason: A natural three-beat list; 'vula' is how speakers say switch on, and 'ulinde' closes it calmly.

rows.en: The car's heater is the most important relationship in your life right now.
rows.draft: I-heater yemoto yiyona relationship ebaluleke kakhulu empilweni yakho njengamanje.
rows.reason: "relationship" is dropped in bare, with no i- prefix, where isiZulu has the everyday word ubudlelwano; the natives swap an English content phrase for the isiZulu word (setting yasebusika, ibhodlela lobisi).
rows.rewrite: I-heater yemoto iwubudlelwano obubaluleke kakhulu empilweni yakho njengamanje.

rows.en: Nobody told the forecast. It just arrived.
rows.reason: "Sivele safika" takes the si- of isibikezelo (or reads as 'we just arrived'), so it says the forecast arrived, not the weather; the weather has to be the one that arrives.
rows.rewrite: Akekho otshele isibikezelo. Izulu livele lafika.

rows.en: Layer up like you're climbing Sani Pass.
rows.draft: Gqoka izingubo eziningi njengokukhwela uSani Pass.
rows.reason: "njengokukhwela uSani Pass" is stiff: u- is the prefix for a person's name, and a speaker would say 'sengathi ukhuphuka i-Sani Pass' (as if you're going up).
rows.rewrite: Gqoka izingubo eziningi sengathi ukhuphuka i-Sani Pass.

rows.en: Rain's possible. So is being completely wrong.
rows.draft: Imvula iyenzeka. Nokungabi yikho nhlobo kuyenzeka.
rows.reason: "Nokungabi yikho nhlobo" means 'it not being so at all'; the English joke is that we, the forecast, could be completely wrong, and that self-dig is lost.
rows.rewrite: Imvula iyenzeka. Nokuthi sibe nephutha ngokuphelele kuyenzeka.

rows.en: The car seats are freezing. Everything is freezing.
rows.draft: Izihlalo zemoto ziyaqanda. Yonke into iyaqanda.
rows.reason: Natural; -qanda is the confirmed word for biting cold (kuyaqanda), and repeating it gives the second beat its escalation.

rows.en: The morning forgot to render.
rows.reason: "Ekuseni" is the adverb 'in the morning', so the line has no clear actor ('in the morning it forgot'); a speaker would name this morning, and the tech loan reads better kept as uku-render, the way natives keep i-startile.
rows.rewrite: Ekuseni kwanamuhla kukhohliwe uku-render.

rows.en: Partly cloudy, partly guessing.
rows.reason: "kuqagela" has no one doing the guessing ('it guesses'); with 'siqagela' the app owns the guess, and the parallel with 'kunamafu kancane' still holds.
rows.rewrite: Kunamafu kancane, siqagela kancane.

rows.en: Perfect weather for pretending you'll go to bed early.
rows.draft: Isimo sezulu esihle sokuzenza uzolala kusenesikhathi.
rows.reason: "sokuzenza uzolala" is missing 'sengathi': a speaker says 'ukuzenza sengathi' for pretending that something is so; the rest is the confirmed 'Isimo sezulu esihle se-' pattern.
rows.rewrite: Isimo sezulu esihle sokuzenza sengathi uzolala kusenesikhathi.

rows.en: A hoodie and an attitude. That's today.
rows.reason: Natural, and 'isimo sengqondo' for attitude is already native-confirmed ('Isimo sengqondo siyaphoqeleka'); 'Namuhla kunje' is easy speech. Some of the sass is lost.

rows.en: Solidarity to everyone with one wet shoe right now.
rows.draft: Ukuhlangana nabo bonke abanesicathulo esisodwa esimanzi manje.
rows.reason: "Ukuhlangana nabo" means 'meeting with them', not solidarity; a speaker would say 'sime nani' (we stand with you), and the rest of the line is fine.
rows.rewrite: Sime nani nonke eninesicathulo esisodwa esimanzi manje.

rows.en: The dams are doing a happy dance.
rows.reason: "enza umdanso ojabulayo" is a word-for-word calque of 'doing a happy dance'; a speaker would just make the dams dance (ayagida) with joy.
rows.rewrite: Amadamu ayagida ngenjabulo.

rows.en: Somewhere out there is the road. We think.
rows.reason: "kunomgwaqo" is 'there is a road' (some road), not 'the road', and on its own 'Sicabanga' reads as 'we are thinking', not 'we think so'.
rows.rewrite: Umgwaqo ukhona ngaphandle, endaweni ethile. Sicabanga kanjalo.

rows.en: Highveld winter: the only place where you wear two jackets to fetch the post.
rows.draft: I-Highveld winter: indawo lapho ugqoka ama-jacket amabili uyolanda iposi.
rows.reason: "I-Highveld winter" is the bare English compound the natives replace (cf. 'setting yasebusika'); 'only' is missing; and 'ama-jacket' should be 'amajazi', the word the confirmed lines use.
rows.rewrite: Ubusika base-Highveld: yiyo kuphela indawo lapho ugqoka khona amajazi amabili uyolanda iposi.

rows.en: The sky's having a full-on tantrum.
rows.reason: Natural and correct; 'sithukuthele ngempela' makes the sky a furious character. The toddler shade of 'tantrum' softens to plain anger, but the line still lands.

rows.en: The sky's giving absolutely nothing.
rows.reason: Plain, natural negative ('asiniki lutho'); the sky giving nothing carries straight over for a flat grey day.

rows.en: The commute just became a team sport.
rows.reason: Natural; on a rainy-traffic day 'uhambo' stands in for the commute, and 'seluphenduke umdlalo weqembu' turns the second beat cleanly.

rows.en: Your out-of-office is doing the heavy lifting.
rows.reason: The natives already keep 'i-out-of-office' ('Ilanga lithumele i-out-of-office'), and 'yenza umsebenzi onzima' is the natural way to say heavy lifting.

rows.en: The streetlights are trying their best.
rows.reason: "zizama ngakho konke" is a calque of 'trying their all' and reads loose ('ngakho' also means 'therefore'); a speaker would say 'ngamandla azo onke'.
rows.rewrite: Izibani zomgwaqo zizama ngamandla azo onke.

rows.en: The car coughed twice before it agreed to start.
rows.draft: Imoto ikhwehlele kabili ngaphambi kokuvuma uku-starta.
rows.reason: The coughing car is a lovely bit of personification, 'ikhwehlele kabili' is natural, and 'uku-starta' matches the confirmed 'i-startile'.

rows.en: Perfect day. No excuses. Get out.
rows.reason: Three clean beats; 'Akukho zaba' correctly drops the vowel after akukho, and 'Phuma' is a natural command.

rows.en: Driving slow is not a suggestion.
rows.reason: Correct and natural; 'akusona isiphakamiso' keeps the dry, firm tone of the English.

rows.en: The pool is not optional.
rows.reason: "Ipuli alikho ukukhetha" reads as 'the pool isn't there, choosing': 'alikho' means 'is absent', so the line says the opposite of a must-swim day, and 'ipuli' is not how people say pool (i-pool).
rows.rewrite: Ukungena e-pool namuhla kuyaphoqeleka.

rows.en: Probably brewing something. Stay close to a roof.
rows.draft: Cishe kukhona okuphekwayo. Hlala eduze nophahla.
rows.reason: 'kukhona okuphekwayo' is the natural isiZulu 'something's cooking', and the second sentence is the native-confirmed 'Hlala eduze nophahla'.

rows.en: The kids still going to school in shorts. They know things we don't.
rows.draft: Izingane zisaya esikoleni ngama-shorts. Ziyazi izinto thina esingazazi.
rows.reason: Natural object relative ('izinto thina esingazazi'); 'zisaya' carries 'still going', and the knowing-kids turn lands.

rows.en: Respect the thunder. It's earned it.
rows.reason: 'Kukufanele' reads as 'it suits you / it's right for you', so the turn about the thunder having earned respect is lost; bare 'ukuduma' is also thinner than 'ukuduma kwezulu'.
rows.rewrite: Hlonipha ukuduma kwezulu. Kufanelwe yikho.

rows.en: Eskom wishes it had this power.
rows.reason: Plain and natural; 'amandla' carries both strength and power, so the Eskom jab works.

rows.en: Ponytail holders are doing overtime.
rows.reason: 'Izibopho zezinwele' is a clear plain phrase for hair ties, and 'zisebenza ngokweqile' (overworking) carries the overtime joke.

rows.en: The fynbos is loving it. You should too.
rows.reason: 'Iyakuthanda' with no object reads as 'it loves you', not 'it loves this weather'; 'Nawe kufanele' then dangles.
rows.rewrite: I-fynbos iyasithanda lesi simo sezulu. Nawe kufanele usithande.

rows.en: Your makeup has an expiry date of 9am.
rows.draft: I-makeup yakho inesikhathi esiphelelayo sangu-9 ekuseni.
rows.reason: 'Esiphelelayo' is a malformed form for 'expiring' and 'isikhathi sangu-9' is stiff; a speaker says the makeup 'iphelelwa yisikhathi ngo-9'.
rows.rewrite: I-makeup yakho iphelelwa yisikhathi ngo-9 ekuseni.

rows.en: Lightning's putting on a show — watch from the window.
rows.reason: 'Uveza umboniso' (reveals a display) is a stiff collocation; the confirmed line has the natives' phrase 'ubeka umbukiso'.
rows.rewrite: Umbani ubeka umbukiso — bukela ngewindi.

rows.en: Calm night, most likely. The sky reserves the right to change.
rows.reason: Natural; matches the confirmed low-confidence pattern ('Iqiniso lingahluka'), though 'reserves the right' flattens to 'might change'.

rows.en: Days like this should come with a soundtrack.
rows.reason: 'Izinsuku ezinje' as in the confirmed lines; 'zize ne-soundtrack' is how people code-switch it.

rows.en: Hot-ish, likely. Keep the water close.
rows.reason: Plain and caring; 'Kushisa cishe' even catches the hot-ish hedge, 'Gcina amanzi eduze' is natural.

rows.en: The braai is cancelled. Yes, really.
rows.reason: 'Kukhanselelwe' is the applicative form ('cancelled for someone'); the plain passive is 'kukhanseliwe'.
rows.rewrite: Ukosa kukhanseliwe. Yebo, ngempela.

rows.en: The kind of day Joburg pretends it doesn't have until you're standing in it.
rows.draft: Uhlobo losuku iJoburg ezenza sengathi alukho, kuze kube usume phakathi kwalo.
rows.reason: Long but grammatical object relative ('iJoburg ezenza sengathi alukho'); the 'until you're standing in it' turn survives.

rows.en: Tan lines are not a personality trait.
rows.reason: 'Imigqa yokushisa' means heat lines, not tan lines, and 'ubuntu' means humanity, not personality: the line says 'heat lines are not ubuntu'.
rows.rewrite: Ama-tan lines akuyona into yokuziqhayisa ngayo.

rows.en: Your hairstyle? Gone. Accept it.
rows.reason: Three short beats a speaker would say; 'Sihambile' for 'gone' and 'Yamukela' as in the confirmed beige line.

rows.en: Eskom-friendly weather. No solar today.
rows.draft: Isimo sezulu esilungele i-Eskom. Akukho solar.
rows.reason: 'Esilungele i-Eskom' carries Eskom-friendly and 'Akukho solar' is the everyday loan; the cloudy-day joke reads.

rows.en: Probably a clear night. The stars haven't confirmed.
rows.reason: Natural; 'azikaqinisekisi' gives the stars the same voice as the confirmed 'asikaqinisekiswa' line.

rows.en: Your steering wheel is a hot plate.
rows.reason: 'Isitsha esishisayo' is a hot dish or bowl, not a hot plate; the stove image is what makes it burn.
rows.rewrite: Isitelingi sakho sesiyisitofu.

rows.en: Africa's sky just hits different.
rows.reason: 'Sihlukile nje' is exactly how a speaker says 'just hits different'.

rows.en: Wet socks. The ultimate betrayal.
rows.reason: 'Amasokisi amanzi' like the confirmed 'ijiyini emanzi'; 'ukukhaphela okukhulu' keeps the betrayal beat.

rows.en: Outside has betrayed you and you went anyway.
rows.draft: Ngaphandle kukukhaphele futhi noma kunjalo uhambile.
rows.reason: 'Futhi noma kunjalo uhambile' stacks two connectives and 'uhambile' (you left) is weaker than 'uphumile' (you went out).
rows.rewrite: Ngaphandle kukukhaphele, kodwa uphumile noma kunjalo.

rows.en: The ceiling fan is doing its best, but its best is not enough.
rows.draft: Ifeni yophahla yenza okusemandleni ayo, kodwa okusemandleni ayo akwanele.
rows.reason: 'Yenza okusemandleni ayo' is the real idiom for doing its best, and the repeat lands the turn; 'ifeni yophahla' is understood.

rows.en: The sun is personally attacking you.
rows.reason: 'Likuhlasela wena mathupha' (attacking you, in person) is natural emphasis and keeps the sun as a character.

rows.en: The braai is happening. The braai always happens. We just pull the chairs closer.
rows.draft: I-braai iyenzeka. I-braai ihlala yenzeka. Sidonsa nje izihlalo zisondele.
rows.reason: Natural three-beat build; i-braai is the loan people use, and 'sidonsa nje izihlalo zisondele' carries the stubborn-braai warmth.

rows.en: Lightning's putting Eskom's grid to shame.
rows.reason: 'Ukubeka ehlazweni' is a real idiom for putting to shame; lightning shaming Eskom lands without naming the grid.

rows.en: Tomorrow's weather is tomorrow's problem.
rows.reason: 'sinkinga' drops the copula: it is 'siyinkinga' or, more naturally, 'yinkinga' (it is tomorrow's problem).
rows.rewrite: Isimo sezulu sakusasa yinkinga yakusasa.

rows.en: Your driveway is a mystery novel right now.
rows.draft: Indlela yakho yokungena iyinoveli yemfihlo manje.
rows.reason: Translated: 'indlela yakho yokungena' reads as 'your way of getting in', and 'inoveli yemfihlo' is a word-for-word 'secret novel'; a speaker says the driveway is now a mystery (imfihlakalo).
rows.rewrite: I-driveway yakho manje iyimfihlakalo.

rows.en: Watch for fog — it likes to arrive unannounced.
rows.draft: Qaphela inkungu — ithanda ukufika ingazange yazise.
rows.reason: 'ingazange yazise' is stiff and has no object; the everyday word for arriving unannounced is 'ngokungazelele'.
rows.rewrite: Qaphela inkungu — ithanda ukufika ngokungazelele.

rows.en: Rain on the way, give or take.
rows.reason: Same shape as the confirmed 'Usuku olufudumele luyeza, cishe'; plain and natural, 'cishe' carries 'give or take'.

rows.en: Hail's down — cover the bakkie.
rows.reason: 'vala' means close/shut, not cover; cover is 'mboza' (as in isembozo). Hail is usually said to 'na', not 'wa'.
rows.rewrite: Isichotho siyana — mboza ibakkie.

rows.en: Could rain. Could just threaten to.
rows.reason: 'Kungasongela nje' has no subject that can threaten (impersonal ku-); give the threat to the sky, and use the confirmed 'Kungase line' for might rain.
rows.rewrite: Kungase line. Noma izulu lingasongela nje.

rows.en: Your washing just moved to the neighbour's yard.
rows.draft: Izingubo zakho zisanda kuthuthela egcekeni likamakhelwane.
rows.reason: 'zisanda kuthuthela' (just relocated) gives the washing a house move; idiomatic and funny, possessive correct.

rows.en: The neighbourhood cats have taken over.
rows.reason: 'akhelwane' is a malformed possessive (should be 'omakhelwane'), and 'asethathile' only means 'have taken' — 'taken over' is 'sebethathe izintambo'.
rows.rewrite: Amakati omakhelwane asethathe izintambo.

rows.en: Saturday energy: maximum. Responsibilities: minimum.
rows.reason: Colon list reads like the confirmed 'Izinhlelo zanamuhla: hlala ngaphandle'; concords right, high/low contrast lands.

rows.en: Sky's throwing rocks. Stay inside.
rows.reason: 'silahla' means throws away/discards; pelting is 'jikijela'. 'Hlala phakathi' should be 'hlala ngaphakathi' as in the confirmed storm line.
rows.rewrite: Isibhakabhaka sijikijela amatshe. Hlala ngaphakathi.

rows.en: Save this one in the memory bank.
rows.reason: 'Gcina lolu suku enkumbulweni' is what a speaker says; warm, the memory-bank image becomes plain memory without loss.

rows.en: The fog arrived unannounced. Classic fog.
rows.reason: 'Inkungu yoqobo' means authentic/original fog, not 'classic' in the typical-of-it sense; the house word for that is 'njengenjwayelo'.
rows.rewrite: Inkungu ifike ingamenyiwe. Njengenjwayelo yayo.

rows.en: Fire up the Weber. It's the law.
rows.reason: 'Basa' is the right verb for lighting a fire, 'Kungumthetho' lands the deadpan; brand stays as is.

rows.en: Mist building, maybe. Headlights wouldn't hurt.
rows.reason: 'Layita izibani' is slangy and turns the gentle 'wouldn't hurt' into an order; people say 'vula izibani', and 'kungcono' keeps the soft advice.
rows.rewrite: Inkungu iyakheka, mhlawumbe. Kungcono uvule izibani zemoto.

rows.en: The fog ate the neighbourhood.
rows.reason: Matches the confirmed 'Inkungu iphuze intaba'; 'idle indawo' is short and the fog-as-eater image lands.

rows.en: Everyone with a pool just became very popular.
rows.draft: Bonke abanepuli basanda kuba nesithunzi kakhulu.
rows.reason: 'isithunzi' means dignity/prestige (and shade), not popular — the line now says pool owners gained dignity; 'ipuli' is not the word people use, they say i-pool.
rows.rewrite: Bonke abane-pool basanda kuthola abangane abaningi.

rows.en: Nature just reminded us of the pecking order.
rows.draft: Imvelo isanda kusikhumbuza ukuthi ubani ophambili.
rows.reason: Echoes the confirmed 'sisikhumbuza ukuthi ubani ongumphathi'; 'ubani ophambili' carries the pecking order naturally.

rows.en: The sun's bunking today.
rows.reason: 'liyabaleka' alone means the sun is fleeing; bunking needs the duty it ran from — 'ukubaleka emsebenzini'.
rows.rewrite: Ilanga libalekile emsebenzini namuhla.

rows.en: Walking to the bin is now an expedition.
rows.reason: 'isikhongelo' is not the everyday word for a rubbish bin — people say umgqomo; 'uhambo olude' gives the expedition its weight.
rows.rewrite: Ukuya emgqomweni manje sekuwuhambo olude.

rows.en: Probably fog later. The Boland does this.
rows.draft: Cishe inkungu kamuva. I-Boland yenza lokhu.
rows.reason: Same pattern as the confirmed 'Cishe kuyaqanda. I-Boland yenza lokhu ekuseni'; natural and clear.

rows.en: Your motivation froze on the way to the door.
rows.draft: Ugqozi lwakho luqande endleleni eya emnyango.
rows.reason: 'Ugqozi' is the confirmed word for motivation, concords right; motivation going cold on the way to the door lands.

rows.en: Walking to the car counts as a sun hazard today.
rows.draft: Ukuhamba uye emotweni kubhekwa njengengozi yelanga namuhla.
rows.reason: Clear and grammatical; 'kubhekwa njengengozi yelanga' is a touch formal but carries 'counts as a sun hazard' and the exaggeration comes through.

rows.en: Your suede shoes chose today? Bold.
rows.draft: Izicathulo zakho zesuede zikhethe namuhla? Isibindi.
rows.reason: 'zikhethe namuhla' reads as 'they chose, today' rather than 'chose today of all days'; 'zesuede' needs the hyphen (ze-suede); bare 'Isibindi.' (courage) is stiff as a reaction, a speaker says 'Unesibindi.'
rows.rewrite: Izicathulo zakho ze-suede zikhethe ukuphuma namuhla? Unesibindi.

rows.en: Perfect night to actually see the Milky Way.
rows.reason: 'iNdlela yoSisi' means 'the sister's road', not the Milky Way; isiZulu has uMthala. 'actually' is also dropped.
rows.rewrite: Ubusuku obuhle kakhulu bokubona uMthala ngempela.

rows.en: Grey skies, low conviction.
rows.reason: 'ukholo' is religious faith, not a forecaster's conviction; 'low faith' reads odd. A speaker says ukuqiniseka (certainty).
rows.rewrite: Izulu limpunga, ukuqiniseka kuphansi.

rows.en: Getting out of bed was a mistake. A documented one.
rows.reason: Natural two beats; 'Elibhaliwe phansi' agrees with iphutha and gives the dry 'on record' turn. Ukuvuka for getting up is everyday usage.

rows.en: Braai weather, boet! No excuses.
rows.reason: 'Izulu lokosa' is how people say braai weather; 'Akukho zaba' is correct (izaba drops its vowel after akukho) and boet stays as the code-switch.

rows.en: Bring a jacket. Or sunscreen. Or both.
rows.draft: Letha ijazi. Noma isivikelo selanga. Noma kokubili.
rows.reason: 'Letha' means bring here (towards the speaker); for taking a jacket along a speaker says 'Phatha' or 'Thatha', as the confirmed lines do.
rows.rewrite: Phatha ijazi. Noma isivikelo selanga. Noma kokubili.

rows.en: Ice cream isn't a treat. It's survival.
rows.reason: 'isipho' means a gift, not a treat; 'Yikuphila' is the wrong copula for ukuphila and 'life' is not 'survival' (ukusinda).
rows.rewrite: I-ice cream akusiyo into emnandi nje. Yindaba yokusinda.

rows.en: A perfectly average sky doing perfectly average things.
rows.draft: Isibhakabhaka esiphakathi nendawo esenza izinto eziphakathi nendawo.
rows.reason: 'phakathi nendawo' is the natives' own word for in-between/average and the repetition carries the deadpan; 'perfectly' is lost but nothing is wrong.

rows.en: You could fry an egg on the N1.
rows.reason: Short and clear; 'bhaka' rather than 'thosa' for fry, but the confirmed 'Ungabhaka isteki epavimentini' shows natives let it stand. N1 keeps the SA anchor.

rows.en: Table Mountain? What Table Mountain?
rows.reason: 'Iyiphi i-Table Mountain?' is exactly how a speaker plays dumb; the place name stays as a code-switch.

rows.en: Blue sky, warm breeze. The simple stuff.
rows.draft: Isibhakabhaka esiluhlaza, umoya ofudumele. Izinto ezilula.
rows.reason: Plain and warm; 'isibhakabhaka esiluhlaza, umoya ofudumele' reads naturally and 'Izinto ezilula' carries the simple-pleasures turn.

rows.en: Even the geyser is putting in extra hours.
rows.reason: Same 'Ngisho ne-' shape as the confirmed lines; i-geyser as loan and 'amahora engeziwe' are natural, and the geyser-as-worker joke lands.

rows.en: The shade is working harder than you today.
rows.reason: Mirrors the confirmed 'Iketela lisebenza ngamandla kunabo bonke namuhla'; natural, and the jab at the reader lands.

rows.en: Sunscreen is not optional, boet.
rows.reason: 'ayikhona' means 'it is not there', so the line reads 'the sun cream isn't there, choosing'; a speaker says 'akusiyo into yokukhetha'. The confirmed lines use isivikelo selanga for sunscreen.
rows.rewrite: Isivikelo selanga akusiyo into yokukhetha, boet.

rows.en: The koppies look like a postcard. Your feet feel like ice blocks.
rows.draft: Ama-koppies abukeka njenge-postcard. Izinyawo zakho zizwakala njenge-ice blocks.
rows.reason: 'Ama-koppies' forces an Afrikaans loan where isiZulu says amagquma; 'zizwakala njenge-ice blocks' is a translated 'feel like' plus an English loan, a speaker says the feet are cold like ice.
rows.rewrite: Amagquma abukeka njenge-postcard. Izinyawo zakho zibanda njengeqhwa.

rows.en: Probably grey. Could lift, could thicken.
rows.reason: Impersonal 'Kungaphakama' (it could rise) does not say the cloud lifts; a reader cannot tell what rises. Name the clouds.
rows.rewrite: Cishe kumpunga. Amafu angasuka, noma angajiya.

rows.en: The world just... disappeared.
rows.reason: Same 'nje...' pause the natives kept in 'Akudabukisi. Nje...'; 'wanyamalala' gives the sudden vanishing.

rows.en: Mixed bag out there. We're hedging.
rows.reason: Natural and matches the low-confidence register of the kept lines; 'hedging' flattens to 'not sure' but the meaning holds.

rows.en: Tiny ice bombs falling. Indoors is the only plan.
rows.draft: Amabhomu eqhwa amancane ayawa. Phakathi yiyo kuphela inhlelo.
rows.reason: 'inhlelo' is not a word (plan is uhlelo), so 'yiyo' agrees with nothing; 'Phakathi' is 'in the middle', indoors is ngaphakathi.
rows.rewrite: Amabhomu amancane eqhwa ayawa. Uhlelo olulodwa: hlala ngaphakathi.

rows.en: The clouds RSVP'd 'maybe' and showed up anyway.
rows.draft: Amafu aphendule athi 'mhlawumbi' avele eza nje.
rows.reason: 'mhlawumbi' is the isiXhosa spelling, isiZulu is mhlawumbe; 'avele eza nje' loses the 'anyway' contrast, needs kodwa.
rows.rewrite: Amafu aphendule athi 'mhlawumbe', kodwa avele afika.

rows.en: The duvet is calling and the duvet is winning.
rows.reason: 'iyaphumelela' means succeeds/passes; for winning a tug-of-war a speaker says 'iyanqoba'.
rows.rewrite: I-duvet iyabiza, futhi i-duvet iyanqoba.

rows.en: Could go misty. The dew point's flirting with it.
rows.reason: First beat is right, but 'Qaphela' (be careful) replaces the dew-point joke with a warning the English never gives; the second beat needs a playful turn.
rows.rewrite: Kungaba nenkungu. Izulu lisayicabanga.

rows.en: Visibility: basically zero.
rows.reason: Same deadpan 'Ukubonakala:' frame as the kept 'ama-vibes kuphela' line; iqanda is the everyday isiZulu zero (scores), cishe carries 'basically'.

rows.en: Breezy, probably. Maybe more.
rows.reason: 'okwengeziwe' is form/officialese ('additional') and does not agree with umoya; a speaker says 'nangaphezulu' for 'maybe more'.
rows.rewrite: Kunomoya omncane, cishe. Mhlawumbe nangaphezulu.

rows.en: Cold enough for soup. And a second soup.
rows.reason: 'Kubanda ngokwanele kwesobho' is a word-for-word 'cold enough for soup' (the possessive kwesobho does not express purpose); a speaker uses kangangokuthi, as the natives did.
rows.rewrite: Kubanda kangangokuthi ufuna isobho. Nelesibili.

rows.en: Some wind expected. Strength still TBC.
rows.reason: Plain and correct, same register as the kept 'asikaqinisekiswa' storm line; 'umoya othile' is slightly vague but natural enough.

rows.en: The traffic lights are vibing in the mist.
rows.reason: 'ziyavuma' means 'they agree / say yes', not 'vibing', so the lights end up agreeing in the fog; locative of inkungu is 'enkungwini', not 'enkungu'.
rows.rewrite: Izibani zomgwaqo zizijabulisa nje enkungwini.

rows.en: Everything looks like a film scene. A creepy one.
rows.draft: Yonke into ibukeka njengomfanekiso wefilimu. Eyesabekayo.
rows.reason: 'umfanekiso' is a picture/illustration, not a film scene; speakers say 'i-scene', and the corpus word for creepy is 'yesabisayo'; 'Konke kubukeka' is the attested phrasing.
rows.rewrite: Konke kubukeka njenge-scene yefilimu. Eyesabisayo.

rows.en: Nobody signed up for this temperature.
rows.reason: Literal but sound: 'izinga lokushisa' is the standard word for temperature and 'akekho ozibhalisele' keeps the bureaucratic joke, like the natives' kept calques.

rows.en: The sky's giving everything today.
rows.reason: Grammatical and warm; the slang 'giving' goes literal but 'the sky gives everything today' still reads as a generous sky, as in the kept 'sinikeza ... amandla' line.

rows.en: Looks wet. The models are fairly sure, not certain.
rows.draft: Kubukeka kumanzi. Amamodeli aqinisekile cishe, hhayi ngokugcwele.
rows.reason: Matches the natives' own low-confidence wording ('Siqinisekile cishe'); 'hhayi ngokugcwele' carries 'not certain' cleanly.

rows.en: Your shoes are about to have a bad day.
rows.reason: Natural and correct; the shoes as a character with a bad day lands in isiZulu.

rows.en: Your car seat is a weapon right now.
rows.reason: Mirrors the kept 'Umnyango wemoto yakho usanda kuba yisikhali'; correct concords, the weapon joke carries.

rows.en: The car is out there. Allegedly.
rows.reason: 'Kuthiwa nje' is exactly how a speaker says 'allegedly'; echoes the kept fog car line.

rows.en: You'll dry. Eventually. Probably.
rows.reason: 'Uzokoma' said to a person reads first as 'you'll be thirsty' (ukoma = thirst), not 'you'll dry'; put it on the clothes so 'oma' means dry.
rows.rewrite: Izingubo zakho zizokoma. Ekugcineni. Cishe.

rows.en: Sun's out. Don't be fooled. Nature is lying.
rows.draft: Ilanga liphumile. Ungakhohliswa. Imvelo iqamba amanga.
rows.reason: Natural three-beat line; 'Ungakhohliswa' and 'iqamba amanga' are idiomatic and the turn lands.

rows.en: Silent Hill vibes. Without the monsters. Hopefully.
rows.draft: I-Silent Hill vibes. Ngaphandle kwezimanga. Sithemba.
rows.reason: 'izimanga' means marvels/wonders, not monsters (use izilo), so the turn says the wrong thing; standalone 'we hope' needs -ya-: 'Siyathemba'.
rows.rewrite: I-Silent Hill vibes. Ngaphandle kwezilo. Siyathemba.

rows.en: Night looks calm. Models permitting.
rows.draft: Ubusuku bubukeka buzolile. Uma amamodeli evuma.
rows.reason: Correct and natural; 'Uma amamodeli evuma' gives the dry 'models permitting' turn, same register as the kept 'Kubukeka kuzolile. Cishe.'

rows.en: Welkom-cold today. The kind that goes through three jerseys like they aren't there.
rows.draft: Kubanda okweWelkom namuhla. Amakhaza angena kuma-jersey amathathu sengathi awekho.
rows.reason: isiZulu has its own word for jersey (ijezi), so 'kuma-jersey' should be 'emajezini' (the natives swap loans for the Zulu word); a place comparison wants 'okwaseWelkom'.
rows.rewrite: Kubanda okwaseWelkom namuhla. Amakhaza angena emajezini amathathu sengathi awekho.

rows.en: The sky can't make up its mind. Join the club.
rows.reason: 'Joyina iklabhu' forces the English idiom into isiZulu and nobody says it; 'ukuzinquma' is off where the natives wrote 'ukunquma'; 'we can't either' carries the turn, like the kept 'Asazi nathi'.
rows.rewrite: Isibhakabhaka asikwazi ukunquma. Nathi asikwazi.

rows.en: Today's weather: still loading.
rows.reason: 'sisalayisha' is the everyday loan for loading, same move as the kept 'siyabafura'; the joke carries.

rows.en: Cloud cover with a side of who-cares.
rows.reason: 'uhlangothi' is a physical side/flank, not a side dish, so 'a side of who-cares' comes out as nonsense; 'ubani onendaba' is right and can carry the line alone.
rows.rewrite: Amafu, kodwa ubani onendaba?

rows.en: Visibility sponsored by nobody.
rows.reason: 'kuxhaswe ngubani. Muntu.' reads 'sponsored by whom? Person.': 'muntu' is not 'nobody', and a reader cannot recover the joke.
rows.rewrite: Ukubonakala: akekho okuxhasile.

rows.en: Somewhere a roof is someone's new kite.
rows.reason: 'umkhumbi' means ship, not kite (the app's recorded error), so the roof becomes a new ship; 'someone's' is also dropped.
rows.rewrite: Endaweni ethile uphahla seluyi-kite entsha yomuntu.

rows.en: Hotter than a bakkie dashboard at noon.
rows.reason: Natural comparison with the bakkie kept as a loan; 'emini' is the right time word and the heat image carries.
